source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio campus publishes 36 MW of IT load, fourth among Texas facilities that disclose capacity, but its certifications describe regulated enterprise workloads rather than AI training.

The campus covers three facilities, SAT2 through SAT4, with 295,785 square feet of technical space. Its published qualifications are PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942. That set is built for finance, healthcare, and federal tenants, whose demands are audit, isolation, and uptime rather than the rack density and cooling that large AI clusters require. Nothing published here describes GPU density, liquid cooling, or high-density rack support.

Texas is a weak sample for judging data center capacity. Only 19 of 133 mapped facilities in the state publish a capacity figure, so the 475 MW state total and this campus's 7.6% share describe disclosure habits, not the actual distribution of compute. Ranking fourth in a state where most operators publish nothing says little about strategic importance to AI scaling.

The binding constraint on AI is power, and this data does not reach it. There is no interconnection capacity, no utility or generation source, no energization date, and no announced expansion. The suitability score of 68 is computed from published IT capacity and operator type alone, and it flags announced expansion as missing. A reader can learn the size and compliance posture of this campus, and nothing about whether it can be powered for AI-scale load.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
